title: Disable System Integrity Protection
summary: System Integrity Protection (SIP) protects system files from modification. Disabling it is a high-risk action usually required only for specific advanced troubleshooting or development tasks, and must be done from Recovery Mode.
prerequisites: Boot into macOS Recovery Mode (Command+R on Intel, hold Power on Apple Silicon)

steps.explain: Run the command to disable System Integrity Protection. This command typically requires execution from Recovery Mode.
steps.expect: Confirmation that SIP has been disabled.

warnings: Disabling SIP reduces system security and stability.
Only disable SIP if you know exactly why you need to.
Re-enable SIP immediately after completing your task.

rollback.explain: Run the command to re-enable System Integrity Protection.
rollback.expect: Confirmation that SIP has been enabled.
